links.comparator_used: Same base LLMs queried without guideline access (paired within-model design); also standard LLMs vs RAG-enhanced Custom GPT
links.outcome: Accuracy (condition-blind LLM judge and human ratings) and content-level hallucination rate on German S3 oral cavity carcinoma guideline questions
links.effect: Judge: hallucination fell from 42% to 4%; pooled accuracy +0.64 points (95% CI 0.47-0.80); +0.48 (95% CI 0.22-0.73) after length adjustment; human ratings +0.61 (95% CI 0.49-0.74). Citation groundedness rose from 0% to 51-89%; retrieval recall@5 92%. Accuracy gain significant in Mistral, Qwen3 and GPT-OSS, directional in DeepSeek and GPT-5.
links.tradeoff: Accuracy gains were small or non-significant for already-strong base models; residual hallucination still requires human oversight; experts could identify retrieval-augmented answers with 98.5% accuracy, compromising blinding of human raters.
links.quote: On the judge, content-level hallucination fell from 42% to 4% and accuracy rose by a pooled +0.64 points (95% CI 0.47-0.80); the accuracy gain persisted after adjustment for response length (+0.48, 95% CI 0.22-0.73), which retrieval shortened rather than lengthened.

links.outcome: Citation groundedness derived deterministically from retrieval logs
